newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle feedlots quiet, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle feedlots quiet, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets Tuesday were inactive, but expected to trade steady to firm Wednesday or Thursday as packers book orders for next week's operations, feedlot sources said.
Packers reportedly held comfortable inventories for this week following brisk purchases the past two weeks, they said.
Light bids early Tuesday at $65.00 per cwt were passed by cattle feeders seeking $67.00 to $68.00, sources said.
Sales this week were seen at $66.00 to $67.00, steady to $1.00 higher, compared with last week's heavy volume. Prices were expected to be underpinned by recent strong beef demand.
Fed cattle prices this week also were seen supported by light supplies of well-finished cattle, sources said.

Early marketing of cattle to meet strong packer demand has kept feedlots current and weights well below a year ago and harsh weather sporting low temperatures last week in the Plains set cattle weight gains back further, sources said.
Feedlots were said to be in good condition, with no mud problems reported in Kansas and the Panhandle.
Light snow cover and strong winds generally kept feedlots dry and prevented them from turning sloppy, sources there said.
